input_case:
History of Present Illness:
50-year-old woman. Persistent right upper abdominal pain and nausea for twenty hours. She previously knew of gallstones but has had no similar prolonged episode.

Physical Examination:
Localized right upper-quadrant guarding and focal inspiratory tenderness. Temperature 37.4 C; heart rate 112/min; BP 116/74 mmHg; respiratory rate 20/min; SpO2 97% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 16.2 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.5 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 248 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 137 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.9 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 81 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 36 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 56 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 47 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 93 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 1.0 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
Ultrasound abdomen: multiple stones, 5 mm gallbladder wall, hyperemia and a small amount of pericholecystic fluid. Common bile duct 4 mm.
